opennyai_summary.arguments:
The petitioner has come before this Court for quashing of the FIR vide Jakkanpur P.S. Case No. 278 of 2020 registered under sections 498A & 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
1 Learned Senior Counsel further submits that later both of them came to a negotiating table which culminated with the dissolution of their marriage vide Matrimonial Case No. 716 of 2021 on 23.4.2022.
Learned Senior Counsel also referred to the order of Supreme Court of India in Rangappa Javoor vs.
The State of Karnataka and Another reported in 2023 Live Law (SC)74 in which Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows:
It is apparent that the parties have resolved and settled their disputes.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS: This court has held that in cases of offences relating to matrimonial disputes, if the Court is satisfied that the parties have genuinely settled the disputes amicably, then for the purpose of securing ends of justice, criminal proceedings inter-se parties can be quashed by exercising the powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India or even under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Issue notice to opposite party no.2
both by registered cover with A/D as well as ordinary process for which requisites etc. must be filed within two weeks from today failing which this application shall stand dismissed without further reference to a Bench.
